reading: The operator recorded in this registry as News-Press & Gazette Company refers to a Bradley family media and investment enterprise whose Omaha, Nebraska data center at 1623 Farnam traces a somewhat complex ownership path. News-Press & Gazette Company, a privately held firm founded in 1951 spanning broadcast television, newspapers, and manufacturing, acquired what was then known as Nebraska Data Centers in 2018 through a new entity called 1623 Farnam LLC, with MVP Capital serving as financial advisor and existing facility president Todd Cushing remaining in place. The new ownership pledged approximately 30 million dollars in capital improvements over five years to develop the site into a carrier-neutral interconnection hub, which today hosts more than 40 network, content, cloud, and IT service providers. Subsequent to that acquisition, the Bradley family sold the majority of NPG's traditional media assets and organized their ongoing investments, including this facility, under a separate vehicle called BERKS Group, so current ownership is best understood as the same family under a different corporate umbrella rather than a change in ultimate control. In February 2025, Fortune reported, based on a footnote in a contract between Trump Media & Technology Group and vendor WorldConnect Technologies, that this Omaha facility hosts a Truth Social data center that became operational around August 2024, noting that Trump Media typically redacts such facility references from its own SEC filings and that Fortune's finding came from the WorldConnect contract rather than direct company disclosure. This registry records that reporting as a well-sourced factual detail without further characterization.
